solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl’s flash director?

blocks.note: Joy is a girl's name, plus the possessive S
in a flash, in a tick: both mean a moment

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a girl's camera flash has its own director.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: the stick a pilot or gamer holds steers where things go. A tick is British slang for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A control lever steers an aircraft or game character, so it directs movement in a playful sense.

clue.text: Way to break up month in legitimate manner

indicators.note: breaking something up splits it open so another piece can sit in the gap

blocks.note: a month of the year
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A road is built that splits a month of the calendar in a lawful fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: ST (street) goes into the middle of JULY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting fairly and rightly is acting with good legal or moral grounds, a direct synonym for this adverb.

clue.text: Youth… wrinkly… rusty… gone!

indicators.note: something wrinkly is crumpled out of its smooth shape, so the letters are rumpled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lament that youth has passed: skin wrinkled, body rusty, all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses make it read like a sigh about ageing, but 'wrinkly' is the anagram signal working on the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, and so is a kid or juvenile; the two nouns are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Root, something with valves, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a tuba is a brass instrument played with valves

explanation.surface: A puzzled guess about a plant root being a device fitted with valves.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent that drops the final R, TUBA and TUBER sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a swollen underground stem storing food, loosely called a root in everyday speech.

clue.text: Scent record when in shape

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a cone is a geometric shape
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A perfume sets a record once it is put into a fancy bottle shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is only a link; 'record' here is the written kind, as in a ship's diary, not a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, so the word names a kind of fragrance worn on the skin.

clue.text: Spirit shown by priest when dancing

indicators.note: dancers move around and change places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows real liveliness when he gets up to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The same six letters as the clergyman, shuffled into a French loanword.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is borrowed French for liveliness of mind or wit, matching one sense of spirit as vivacity.

clue.text: Broadcast is done, but it’s a memorable clip

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A programme has finished airing, yet one short excerpt of it lingers in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the media surface so well that it looks like part of the definition; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A short catchy extract from a speech or interview, quoted in news reports, is exactly a remembered snippet of recording.

clue.text: Sly character in mob marched uphill

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters that follows, spanning the word break
in a down clue going uphill means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A cunning figure among a crowd that trudged up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sly' is Sylvester Stallone, whose best-known role was the Vietnam veteran commando; read the hidden letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone, nicknamed Sly, played this action-film hero, so it is a character of the actor's.

clue.text: Aroused, no?

blocks.note: surface reading: a teasing question about whether someone is excited
setter's reading: flip the little word round and you get its mirror, which the phrase itself describes

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for being aroused also describes the clue's last word read backwards: NO reversed is ON, so ON is what 'no' becomes once turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excited, especially sexually, is being switched on; the phrasal verb is an everyday idiom for that state.

clue.text: Young bird qualified after losing head in fight

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so losing it drops the first letter

blocks.note: a squab is a young pigeon
able means competent or qualified

explanation.surface: A fledgling, fully trained, gets knocked on the head during a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: A squab is a pigeon chick; the doubled B in the answer comes from the join of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy petty quarrel is a minor fight, so the noun is a mild synonym for an argument or scrap.

clue.text: Heyday for accountant, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: the peak season of one's life
second meaning: one who adds figures up

explanation.surface: An accountant's busiest, brightest time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a coined word, one who sums, pronounced differently from the season; 'perhaps' warns it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm season stands for one's prime, and an accountant adding numbers could whimsically be called one who does sums.

clue.text: Powder that’s also like chalk, on all surfaces

indicators.note: a surface is the outermost face, so only the leading letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A dusting that resembles chalk and gets over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The mineral powder is itself chalk-like, so the clue half-defines itself as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is a soft mineral ground fine and dusted on skin, so it is a common household powder.

clue.text: Drink, glorious on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word appears backwards

blocks.note: regal means royal, splendid

explanation.surface: Someone thinks back and decides a beer was magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as thinking it over, but here it means mirror-image.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light fizzy beer, one example of an alcoholic beverage ordered in a pub.

clue.text: Majestic bubbly organised

indicators.note: bubbly means fizzing and agitated, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A regal party where the champagne has been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne, the noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something imposing and splendid in scale, though the answer often carries a hint of pomposity.

clue.text: Dropping back, a little help at school essential

indicators.note: to drop back is to go the other way, so the letters are read from the end
only a small part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A pupil who is falling behind finds a bit of extra support at school vital.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside the first word and ends on the first letter of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food or item is a basic necessity, so as a noun it names something essential to daily life.

clue.text: Women’s tights: criticise one wearing the aforementioned items

indicators.note: whoever wears something is inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to pan is to review harshly
those points back to things just named
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A critic slates someone for wearing the tights just described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The aforementioned items' seems to point back to the tights but simply gives a pronoun; 'pan' is the reviewer's verb for a hostile notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for sheer nylon leg-wear joined to briefs is exactly what Britons call tights.

clue.text: US city, voguish earlier

blocks.note: chic means fashionable
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An American city that used to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Two plain synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City on Lake Michigan is the third largest city in America, in Illinois.

clue.text: Law also entering new era for great leader?

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so these pieces sit within the other
a new version is a remade one, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: lex is Latin for law
and adds something, as also does
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new body of law ushers in an age for a mighty ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Lex is the Latin word for law. The question mark signals the pun: the Macedonian king was known as 'the Great'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, king of Macedon, conquered an empire, so he is literally a leader called great.

clue.text: Star hugged by damsel in US city

indicators.note: something hugged is held within arms, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
Vega is a bright star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity is embraced by a young woman in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a showbiz celebrity, fitting the city, but it is an actual star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada gambling resort is one of the best-known cities in America, famed for casinos.

clue.text: Comrade entering in the morning — condensation initially seen?

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a.m. marks the morning hours
a crony is a close companion

explanation.surface: A friend walks in at dawn and notices dew on the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condensation' suggests water on glass, but here it means shortening; the word is formed from first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a word is a shortened term built from the opening letters of a phrase, so it is a compression shown by initials.

clue.text: In conference, come together for food

indicators.note: a conference is a talk between people, so the word is taken as spoken

blocks.note: to meet is to come together

explanation.surface: Delegates at a meeting gather to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conference' fits the business surface; it is what makes the word spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal flesh eaten as a dish is a staple of the diet, so it is a type of nourishment.

clue.text: Game and wine ranked

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
red is a wine

explanation.surface: Venison and claret graded on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like wild meat beside wine; in British sport a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in levels or rows one above another is organised by grade, so the adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Pretty short period for speaker

indicators.note: something short falls short of full length, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: twee is British for affectedly pretty or quaint
a term is a period, as of school

explanation.surface: A lecturer with a brief, rather sweet stint at the lectern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests a person talking; it is a loudspeaker for high frequencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loudspeaker unit that reproduces treble notes is a type of audio speaker in a hi-fi system.

clue.text: Woman after graduation screwed up manual

indicators.note: paper that is screwed up is crumpled out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once she had her degree, a woman crumpled up the textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin feminine form is used for a former female student.
explanation.definitionFit: A female former pupil or graduate of a college is exactly what the Latin feminine noun denotes.

clue.text: Originally valid point, free from suspicion

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to point to something is to indicate it

explanation.surface: A sound argument clears someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as a noun in the surface; the wordplay needs the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame or show them to be right is to exonerate them, the core sense of this verb.

clue.text: Love gathered in by bouquet catcher

indicators.note: something gathered in is drawn inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: At a wedding, a sweetheart is gathered up by the guest who catches the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet catcher' reads as the bridesmaid who catches the flowers; split it and 'bouquet' is the wine term.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop of rope tightens around whatever it snares, so a lasso-style loop is a catcher.

clue.text: Pack up table at market, say

blocks.note: first meaning: of an engine, to stop working
second meaning: a trader's stand

explanation.surface: A trader packs up the stand at the end of market day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack up' is British informal for breaking down, as an engine does.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that cuts out suddenly is said to break down, and a trestle where goods are sold at a fair is a booth.

clue.text: Sharp sting

blocks.note: first meaning: quick-witted or neatly dressed
second meaning: to hurt with a burning pain

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sharp pain, but it is two separate meanings, an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever or crisp describes a keen mind or tidy look, and the verb names a prickling burning pain.

clue.text: Extraordinary number try to get mark reversed

indicators.note: reversed means turned the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
a logo is a brand mark

explanation.surface: An exceptional number of attempts made to score a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is ten to the power of a hundred, source of a search engine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten raised to the hundredth power is an enormous figure, so it is a remarkable quantity in mathematics.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in basic unit, arbitrarily

indicators.note: whatever is invested is placed within something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: an atom is a basic unit of matter
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is put into some fundamental venture without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' fits the financial surface; it simply puts one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without plan or reason is doing it by chance, so the phrase and the adverb match.

clue.text: Country where journalist has broken story after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the letters come round the other way
to break into something is to get inside it

blocks.note: a news story
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter breaks the story of an uprising in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests a political uprising, fitting the reporting scene, but it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scandinavian kingdom with Stockholm as capital is a nation, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Standards erratic, I suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not in proper order, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone voices doubts that quality levels are slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as a shrug; 'suspect' is the anagram signal and 'I' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Benchmarks used for judging something are the principles it is measured by, a close plural synonym.
